name: Aryabhata
tagline: India’s first satellite opened a new chapter, circling Earth long after its first experiments were meant to end.
credit: Original editorial illustration created for the Left Behind archive.

beats.goal: Build and operate India’s first satellite while developing national capability in spacecraft design, fabrication, tracking and control.
beats.achieved: Launched on April 19, 1975, Aryabhata carried experiments in X-ray astronomy, aeronomy and solar physics. Its mainframe operated beyond its nominal six-month design life.
beats.ending: The satellite’s signals ceased after its final tracked orbit, and it re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on February 10, 1992.
beats.now: Aryabhata no longer exists as an orbiting object; it burned up during atmospheric re-entry. Its legacy remains central to India’s space programme.
beats.learned: The mission built essential experience in spacecraft engineering, telemetry, tracking, command operations and scientific payloads.
